argument:
Warrant proceeds are financing, as the bear says, and cannot be labelled recurring earned cash. The more relevant operating counterpoint is that H1 CFO increased from RM50.801m to RM62.623m despite RM80.148m receivables absorption. After RM27.132m capex, RM35.491m cash remained. Thus the growth program has a positive operating contribution separately from the much larger externally augmented liquidity pool.

The RM118m Taiwan capacity program has a disclosed funding route without bank borrowings, although leases and warrant dilution remain economically relevant. Revenue growth of 30% supports utilization potential, while other income qualifies profit growth. At 47.18x trailing earnings, this is a purchase for profitable capacity conversion rather than cash balances alone. The positive inference is that stronger collections and utilization can enlarge per-share returns; neither that outcome nor the forward estimate is established by the warrant raise.
key_points: Operating CFO increased despite receivables absorption.
Positive post-capex cash is separate from warrant funding.
Capacity must generate per-share returns after dilution.
rebuttal_to_previous: The liquidity pool is not wholly operating cash. However, CFO rose by RM11.822m and retained RM35.491m after capex despite receivables absorption. That distinguishes a cash-generating operating expansion from a thesis resting only on financing proceeds, while retaining the dilution hurdle.
